tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

## claude-in-chrome

67	## Implementer rules (read fully before your first task)
68	
69	### R0. Scope
70	
71	- Do only the task you were given and edit only the files it names. If a correct change needs another
72	  file, **stop and ask**.
73	- Line numbers are approximate (base 04555de). Find code by function name.
74	- One task = one commit, message `<area>: <what>` (`fuzz: page target`, `ci: fuzz smoke job`).
75	- Library bugs found while building a harness are **not fixed in the harness task**. Follow R5.
76	
77	### R1. Toolchains and commands (Windows, from the repo root; never `cd` into subdirs)
78	
79	```
80	Z16 = C:/Users/cable/tools/zig-x86_64-windows-0.16.0/zig.exe     # 0.16.0
81	Z17 = zig                                                        # 0.17.0 on PATH
82	make test-lib CODECS=zig-only ZIG=C:/Users/cable/tools/zig-x86_64-windows-0.16.0/zig.exe
83	make test-lib CODECS=zig-only ZIG=zig
84	make fmt ZIG=C:/Users/cable/tools/zig-x86_64-windows-0.16.0/zig.exe   # then `git diff --stat` must show only your files
85	zig ast-check <file.zig>                                             # 0.17 parse check of one file
86	```
87	
88	Targets added by this plan (task 1.1): `make fuzz-run TARGET=<t> [SECONDS=60] [SEED=n]`,
89	`make fuzz-replay TARGET=<t> FILES=<path>`, `make fuzz-cov [N=200K]` (Linux/macOS only).
90	
91	Linux (WSL), for `fuzz-cov`, the `file-oom` lane and anything that "crashed only on Linux":
92	
93	```
94	wsl.exe -e bash -lc 'rsync -a --delete --exclude .zig-cache --exclude zig-out --exclude .zig17 --exclude node_modules --exclude target /mnt/c/Users/cable/Documents/dev/zig-parquet/.claude/worktrees/zig-parquet-perf-compat-dc9ccc/ ~/zp/ && cd ~/zp && make fuzz-cov ZIG=$HOME/zig16/zig N=200K'
95	```
96	
97	Copy trees to `~/zp`, never `/tmp`. WSL has only Zig 0.16, so 0.17 Linux runs happen in CI.
98	
99	- Always pass `CODECS=zig-only` locally (the `fuzz-*` targets default to it). C codecs instrumented
100	  by `--fuzz` do not link (zarrow build.zig:147 learned this), so a `--fuzz` build **must** be
101	  zig-only.
102	- "Tests pass" means 919/919 or higher on both versions, plus the new fuzz tests, with no new skips.
103	
104	### R2. Zig API gotchas (0.16 and 0.17)
105	
106	- `std.ArrayList(T)`: `.empty`, and pass the allocator to every method. In-memory output goes to
107	  `std.Io.Writer.Allocating`.
108	- Files: `std.Io.Dir.cwd().readFileAlloc(io, path, gpa, .limited(n))`, `openDir(io, p, .{ .iterate = true })`,
109	  `it.next(io)`. Copy the exact calls from zarrow `fuzz/fuzz.zig` `listInputs` and `replay`; they compile on both versions.
110	- `std.testing.allocator` and `std.testing.io` are compile errors outside tests. Harness functions
111	  take `gpa: Allocator` and `io: std.Io`, and only `test` blocks pass the testing ones.
112	  `std.testing.FailingAllocator` is fine in the exe.
113	- Executable entry: `pub fn main(init: std.process.Init) !void` (`init.gpa`, `init.io`, `init.arena`,
114	  `init.minimal.args.toSlice(arena)`).
115	
116	### R3. Dual-version rules
117	
118	Use the AGENTS.md table (`@splat`, never `**`; `std.fmt.allocPrint`; `@intFromEnum`/`@enumFromInt`;
119	`std.heap.DebugAllocator(.{})`; no new `std.meta.fields`/`Int`/`Tag`; `std.meta.stringToEnum` is
120	fine). No `builtin.zig_version` gates. `make fmt` only with Z16. **Every task proves both versions
121	the same way:** `make test-lib CODECS=zig-only` with Z16 and with Z17 (the corpus replay is part of
122	`test`), plus the task's own `make fuzz-run ... ZIG=<both>` line for exe changes.
123	
124	### R4. Hardening rules apply to harness code too
125	
126	The harness parses untrusted bytes just as the library does. Never `@intCast` input-derived values;
127	use `Input.below(n)`, `% n` or `safe.castTo`. Every slice of input goes through `Input.rest()` or a
128	bounds check. A harness panic is reported as a library bug, so the harness itself must never panic
129	on input.
130	
131	### R5. When a target finds something
132	
133	1. Save the input. The `run` loop leaves it in `zig-parquet/.fuzz-out/<target>/current.bin`;
134	   `fuzz-cov` leaves it in `<cache>/f/crash` (strip the first 4 bytes: `tail -c +5 crash > input.bin`).
135	2. Minimize it: `python zig-parquet/fuzz/minimize.py <target> input.bin out.bin` (task 1.8).
136	3. Report target, kind (panic message / `fuzz-leak` / `fuzz-oom` / `fuzz-hang` / `mismatch`), the first
137	   `src/` stack frame, and the minimized file. **Do not fix the library in the same task.**
138	4. Fix tasks (separate, owner-approved) follow zarrow `docs/fuzzing.md` "Fix it": fix at the trust
139	   boundary in the shared function. Never loosen validation, catch a panic or special-case the input.
140	   Then promote the input as a regression (R8).
141	5. If the input is a *valid* Parquet file (another engine reads it) and zig-parquet rejects it, that is a
142	   compatibility gap, not a fuzz bug. Add it to `test-files-wild/` with a line in
143	   `expected-failures.txt` and open an issue.
144	
145	### R6. Stop and ask when
146	
147	- a test fails and two honest fix attempts did not fix it;
148	- a change needs a file the task does not list, or a `src/` change (Phase 1-3 tasks touch `src/` only
149	  where named);
150	- the compiler shows a 0.16/0.17 difference that R3 does not cover;
151	- a target produces more than 3 distinct findings in its first 5 minutes (likely a harness bug).
152	
153	### R7. What NOT to do (whole plan)
154	
155	- No new Zig dependencies, no fuzzing frameworks, no Python packages beyond `duckdb` (D6).
156	- No public API changes. Phase 1-3 add nothing to `src/` except task 2.4's internal encoder parameter.
157	- No changes to library defaults (checksums, dictionary, page size) to make a target pass.
158	- No rewrites of zarrow code "to be nicer". Port it, rename it, change only what Parquet needs.
159	
160	### R8. Regression promotion: where findings live (permanent)
161	
162	| Finding | Lives in | Name | Expected behaviour recorded in |
163	|---|---|---|---|
164	| Crash, leak, hang or OOM on some input (any byte target) | `zig-parquet/fuzz/corpus/<target>/` | `regress-<yyyymmdd>-<area>-<slug>.bin` (minimized raw input, not Smith-encoded) | one line in `zig-parquet/fuzz/corpus/expected.txt`: `<target>/<file> ok \| error.<Name> \| error` |
165	| Wrong values from a valid file | `zig-parquet/src/tests/<area>_test.zig` | `test "regress: <slug>"` that builds the minimized case in code; or a ≤ 4 KiB file in `fuzz/corpus/file/` plus an exact-row assertion | the test itself |
166	| Writer bug (round trip or interop) | `zig-parquet/src/tests/writer_*_test.zig` | `test "regress: <slug>"`: write the minimized Case, read it back, compare | the test |
167	| Another engine's bug (xdiff) | `test-files-arrow/xdiff-known.txt` | `<file> <engine> <reason/upstream link>` | that line |
168	
169	`zig build test` replays every corpus file on every CI lane and both Zig versions, and asserts the
170	`expected.txt` outcome exactly. Pinning the error name catches error-class drift as well as crashes.
171	
172	---
173	
174	## Phase 1: byte-level harness, safety oracle (about 3-4 Haiku-days)
175	
176	Goal: every untrusted-input surface gets a target. On every input, the oracle checks that there is
177	no panic, no leak (per-input count), no live allocation over 256 MiB and no hang over 10 s, and
178	that every reader mode agrees when they all succeed. Seeds: the 285 existing small files. Drivers:
179	(a) a seeded mutation loop that works on every OS, including Windows; (b) `std.testing.fuzz`
180	coverage-guided on Linux/macOS; (c) corpus replay inside `zig build test`. One `runOne(target, gpa, bytes)` backs all three.
181	
182	Layout (new files only under `zig-parquet/fuzz/`):
183	
184	```
185	zig-parquet/fuzz/fuzz.zig        CLI (run/replay/gen-seeds), CountingAllocator, runOne, mutate, std.testing.fuzz tests
186	zig-parquet/fuzz/common.zig      Input (decision stream), Feedback, valuesEqual, freeRows
187	zig-parquet/fuzz/t_file.zig      target file / file-oom
188	zig-parquet/fuzz/t_page.zig      target page
189	zig-parquet/fuzz/t_encoding.zig  target encoding
190	zig-parquet/fuzz/t_thrift.zig    target thrift
191	zig-parquet/fuzz/t_codec.zig     target codec
192	zig-parquet/fuzz/corpus/<target>/*.bin, corpus/expected.txt
193	zig-parquet/fuzz/minimize.py     stdlib-only byte minimizer (subprocess per candidate)
194	```
195	
196	### Task 1.1 Scaffold: build steps, Makefile, CLI driver, stub targets

355	  `make fuzz-replay TARGET=file FILES=../test-files-wild ZIG=zig` prints "replayed".
356	  WSL: `make fuzz-cov ZIG=$HOME/zig16/zig N=1K` exits 0 and prints the FUZZING REPORT.
357	- Acceptance: the above, plus `make fmt ZIG=<Z16>` produces no diff and `git status` shows no `.fuzz-out` files.
358	
359	### Task 1.2 ∥ `file` / `file-oom` target: whole-file read, metamorphic across reader modes
360	
361	- Files: `zig-parquet/fuzz/t_file.zig`, `zig-parquet/fuzz/common.zig` (add `valuesEqual`, `freeRows`)
362	- Depends on: 1.1
363	- Change: for `oom`, the first 2 bytes choose `fail_index = int(u16)` (`0xffff` = never fail). Wrap
364	  `gpa` in `std.testing.FailingAllocator.init(gpa, .{ .fail_index = ... })`; the rest of the bytes are the
365	  file. Then:
366	  1. `var r = parquet.openBufferDynamic(a, file, .{ .checksum = .{ .validate_page_checksum = (hash(file) & 7) == 0 } }) catch |e| return e;`
367	     then `defer r.deinit()`.
368	  2. Reference: for each row group `rg < min(getNumRowGroups(), 16)`, `readAllRows(rg)`. Stop at 4096 rows in
369	     total (keep the read bounded). An error ends the target with that error.
370	  3. Each of these must produce rows **equal to the reference** whenever it succeeds without error:
371	     `rowIterator()`, `rowIteratorStreaming()`, and `readRowsProjected(rg, cols)`, where `cols` is
372	     the subset given by the bits of `hash(file)` over the top-level column count. The projected rows
373	     are compared with the matching columns of the reference.
374	     A mode that errors where the reference succeeded is a mismatch **only for OOM-free runs**
375	     (`!oom`); with `oom` set, any mode may hit the injected failure.
376	  4. A mismatch calls `std.debug.panic("fuzz-mismatch: {s} rg {d} row {d} col {d}", ...)`.
377	  5. `fb.rows` = reference row count; `fb.detail` = bit set of modes that succeeded.
378	- `valuesEqual(a: Value, b: Value) bool`: deep equality over all 11 `Value` variants. Floats compare by
379	  bit pattern, except that any NaN equals any NaN. Slices compare by content. Map entries and
380	  struct fields compare in order, and field names must match.
381	  `freeRows(gpa, rows)`: `for (rows) |row| row.deinit(); gpa.free(rows);` (the pattern from roundtrip_test.zig:97-101).
382	- Test: both versions pass. `make fuzz-run TARGET=file SECONDS=60` and `TARGET=file-oom SECONDS=60` on Windows; no
383	  finding is expected, but if there is one, follow R5. Add a unit test in `common.zig` for `valuesEqual` (NaN, -0.0,
384	  nested list vs struct, different field names).
385	- Acceptance: the corpus replay in `zig build test` exercises all ≤ 64 KiB seeds through every mode with
386	  no mismatch, and the whole fuzz test binary adds ≤ 30 s to `make test-lib` in Debug (if it adds more, report the
387	  number; do not drop seeds silently). Note the execs per second printed by `run` in the commit body.

import os
import sys

# usage: mkseeds.py <repo-root> <out-dir>
# Scratch-only: a seed set without parquet-testing/data (which holds large_string_map.brotli.parquet,
# a valid file whose decoded column chunk is over 2 GB and trips the 256 MiB fuzz cap).
root = sys.argv[1].replace("\\", "/")
out = sys.argv[2]
plain = os.path.join(out, "plain")
oom = os.path.join(out, "oom")
os.makedirs(plain, exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(oom, exist_ok=True)
n = 0
for sub in ["test-files-arrow", "test-files-wild"]:
    for dp, _dn, fn in os.walk(os.path.join(root, sub)):
        if "parquet-testing/data" in dp.replace("\\", "/"):
            continue
        for f in fn:
            if not f.endswith(".parquet"):
                continue
            b = open(os.path.join(dp, f), "rb").read()
            if len(b) > 65536:
                continue
            open(os.path.join(plain, "%04d.parquet" % n), "wb").write(b)
            open(os.path.join(oom, "%04d.bin" % n), "wb").write(b"\xff\xff" + b)
            n += 1
print("seeds:", n)

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

# usage: filter.py <zp-fuzz.exe> <seeds-dir> <target> <out-dir>
# Scratch-only: keeps the seeds that replay without a panic (drops the ones that trip the
# known library leak/oom findings so a throughput run can proceed). Prints what it dropped.
exe, src, target, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4]
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
kept = dropped = 0
for name in sorted(os.listdir(src)):
    path = os.path.join(src, name)
    r = subprocess.run([exe, target, "replay", path], capture_output=True)
    if r.returncode == 0:
        shutil.copy(path, os.path.join(out, name))
        kept += 1
    else:
        dropped += 1
        msg = (r.stderr or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines()
        reason = next((l for l in msg if "panic:" in l), "exit %d" % r.returncode)
        print("dropped", name, reason.strip()[:120])
print("kept", kept, "dropped", dropped)
